verses.text: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also from that don’t withdraw your hand; for he who fears God will come out of them all.
Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin.
Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise”; but it was far from me.
That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
“Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find out the scheme;
which my soul still seeks; but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand; but I have not found a woman among all those.
Behold, I have only found this: that God made man upright; but they search for many schemes.”

footnotes.content: A good name—what people carry about you after you've gone—lasts longer than the pleasures that fade. The day we die? It's more honest to face than the day we were born, because by then we know what we've learned and whom we've loved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sorrow teaches what feasting cannot. Standing in a house of grief, we remember that all of us will end, and the living wake up for a moment. It's a hard mercy, this reminder of death.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tears do something laughter cannot—they soften the heart, make it honest. When sorrow marks your face, your spirit learns to see truly. This is the Teacher's paradox: what wounds you also heals you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wise hearts visit the grieving; foolish hearts cling to party noise. The difference between them is not in what they believe, but in where they sit and whom they listen to. Company shapes the soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A rebuke from someone wise stings, but it stays. The song of fools is pleasant at the moment and leaves nothing but air. The sting is a gift if you're humble enough to take it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thorns crackle and spark and are gone—a little sound and flash, then ash. That's what the fool's laughter amounts to: bright noise, burning fast, leaving nothing. The Teacher says plainly: it's all vanity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the wisest can be bent out of shape by taking what isn't theirs. Corruption starts small—a bribe here, an unfair advantage there—and then the mind forgets how to see straight. Guard the door.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The end of a matter shows what it was really made of. And patience—staying steady in spirit while others fume—that's rarer and stronger than pride that flares up quick. The quiet one outlasts the shouter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anger that springs up fast is the fool's chair—he sits in it and it becomes his home. The wise person lets the impulse pass like a cloud. A moment's pause can change everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heart that sighs for the good old days isn't asking wisdom—it's complaining to the wind. Every time had its hard parts and its blessings. The present moment deserves to be met as it is, not measured against a memory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wisdom and an inheritance are both good to have, but wisdom benefits those who see the sun—meaning all of us, all our days. An inheritance passes; wisdom grows and bears fruit across a lifetime.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Both wisdom and money can shelter you, but wisdom does something money cannot—it keeps you alive to yourself, keeps your soul intact. Money protects your body; wisdom protects your life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When God makes something crooked in His plan, no scheme of ours can straighten it. There's a kind of freedom in accepting what we cannot mend—it turns us toward what we can do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prosperity calls for joy; hardship calls for reflection—both are His work, placed side by side. In this balance, we cannot presume to know the whole plan. Seasons teach what certainty never could.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Teacher has seen righteous people suffer and wicked people flourish—it troubles the neat answer. This is not despair but honesty: the world as it is asks us to trust God, not easy outcomes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Strive for righteousness, yes, but not with a grip so tight you strangle yourself. The person who performs perfection destroys themselves with it. There's a wholeness that comes from stepping back and trusting grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't tip toward foolishness or evil either—that's the Teacher's balance. The fool dies before his time not because God cuts him short, but because his own choices close the door. Wisdom is staying in the middle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hold both lessons—hold the call to righteousness and the call to mercy. Don't withdraw your hand from either one. The one who fears God walks this balance and comes through it all, kept by something larger than themselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One truly wise person is stronger than ten officials making noise. Wisdom doesn't shout; it holds steady. In a room full of power, the quiet voice that sees clearly often matters most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not one righteous person on earth who never stumbles. This is liberation disguised as a hard word—if you're waiting to be perfect before you deserve grace, you'll never find it. We're all learners here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't listen to every word spoken about you—especially your servant's curses, the complaints people make when they think you're not listening. Taking them to heart wounds you needlessly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your own heart knows you've said the same cruel things about others. This quiet shame is the Teacher's point—it makes mercy possible. We are all flawed judges of one another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Teacher set out to master wisdom and found he could not master it. The mind that thinks it can capture truth in its palm is always disappointed. Wisdom remains larger than the container we try to make for it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What is, is far away and deep—too distant and too profound to fully reach. This isn't despair; it's the start of genuine seeking. Some mysteries are meant to humble us, not frustrate us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Teacher keeps turning around, looking for the scheme of things. He learns that wickedness is really stupidity, and foolishness is madness—they destroy themselves. Understanding this doesn't solve everything, but it clarifies the cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More bitter than death, the Teacher says, is the woman who sets snares. He speaks from hard experience—seduction that traps the heart is one of life's deepest dangers. Only the one who pleases God escapes; the sinner is caught.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Preacher lays out what he has found: the way things truly work. He's not hiding; he's offering his hard-won observations to those willing to listen and think carefully.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Among a thousand men, one stands out as truly wise; among all the women he's encountered, none met that mark. It's a sober observation, not misogyny—the Teacher is naming his own struggle to find the wisdom he seeks anywhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God made us upright, with the capacity to walk straight with Him. But we keep searching for schemes, shortcuts, ways to bend the system. Readers today hear an echo: how little has changed about the human heart seeking complexity when simplicity is offered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
